title: Brazil Extension
description: Brazilian succession rules: meação (community property split), legítima (forced heirship), inventário process types, cartório attestation, disponível (testamentary freedom portion), and união estável (stable union recognition).
dataProvenance: Brazilian Civil Code (Lei 10.406/2002), Código de Processo Civil (Lei 13.105/2015)

meacao.description: Meação — the surviving spouse's 50% community property entitlement that is separated before succession begins. Not an inheritance share — it is the spouse's own property

applicable.description: Whether meação applies to this estate

propertyRegime.description: The matrimonial property regime governing the meação split
propertyRegime.$comment: comunhao_parcial_de_bens: partial community of property (default regime since 1977). comunhao_universal_de_bens: universal community of property. separacao_total_de_bens: total separation of property. participacao_final_nos_aquestos: participation in final acquisitions.

spousePersonId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the surviving spouse entitled to meação

communityPropertyValue.description: Total value of community property subject to meação split, in minor currency units

legitima.description: Legítima — the mandatory 50% of the estate reserved for compulsory heirs (herdeiros necessários: descendants, ascendants, surviving spouse). Brazilian Civil Code Art. 1.846

compulsoryHeirs.description: Array of persons who are compulsory heirs under Brazilian law

legitimaPortion.description: The legítima portion as a percentage (always 50% under current law)

disponivel.description: Disponível — the freely disposable portion of the estate (50% after legítima). The testator may bequeath this to anyone

portion.description: The disponível portion as a percentage (50% under current law)

estimatedValue.description: Estimated value of the disponível portion in minor currency units

inventarioType.description: Type of inventário (estate inventory and distribution process)
inventarioType.$comment: judicial: mandatory when there are minor heirs, incapacitated heirs, or disputes. extrajudicial: permitted since Lei 11.441/2007 when all heirs are of age, capable, and in agreement — processed at a cartório (notary office). Required in both cases within 60 days of death (CPC Art. 611).

cartorioAttestation.description: Details of notarial attestation at a Brazilian cartório (notary office)

tabeliao.description: Name of the tabelião (notary) who attested the document

livroNumber.description: Book (livro) number in the cartório registry

folhaNumber.description: Page (folha) number in the cartório registry

uniaoEstavel.description: União estável (stable union) — recognised as equivalent to marriage for inheritance purposes under Brazilian law (Art. 1.723 Civil Code). A partner in a stable union has the same inheritance rights as a spouse

recognised.description: Whether the relationship is recognised as a stable union

partnerPersonId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the stable union partner

startDate.description: Approximate start date of the stable union

judicialDeclaration.description: Whether the stable union has been judicially declared

contractRegistered.description: Whether a stable union contract was registered at a cartório

itcmdRate.description: ITCMD (Imposto sobre Transmissão Causa Mortis e Doação) — state-level inheritance tax rate. Varies by state, capped at 8% by the Federal Senate

state.description: Brazilian state abbreviation (e.g. SP, RJ, MG)

progressive.description: Whether the state applies progressive rates
